purpose: Silodosin is used to treat the symptoms of an enlarged prostate, a condition called benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH). It helps relieve problems like difficulty starting urination, weak urine stream, and the need to urinate frequently or urgently. It does not shrink the prostate, but it does help make urinating easier and more comfortable.
how_it_works: Your prostate and bladder neck have tiny receptors called alpha-1 receptors that can cause muscles to tighten and squeeze the urethra, making it hard to pee. Silodosin blocks these receptors, which relaxes those muscles and opens up the pathway so urine can flow more freely. Think of it like loosening a tight valve so water can flow through a pipe more easily.
common_side_effects: The most common side effect is retrograde ejaculation, which means semen goes backward into the bladder instead of out during orgasm — this is harmless but can be surprising. You may also feel dizzy, especially when standing up quickly, so take it slow when getting up. Other side effects can include a stuffy or runny nose, diarrhea, and headache.
warnings: Be careful when standing up from sitting or lying down, as this medicine can cause a sudden drop in blood pressure that may make you feel faint or dizzy — especially when you first start taking it. Tell your doctor if you are taking blood pressure medications, erectile dysfunction drugs like sildenafil or tadalafil, or any other alpha-blockers, as these can increase the risk of low blood pressure. If you ever need cataract or glaucoma eye surgery, let your eye surgeon know you take or have taken this medication, as it can affect the procedure. This medication is only for men and should never be taken by women or children.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is one 8 mg capsule taken once a day with a meal. Taking it with food helps reduce the chance of dizziness. Try to take it at the same time each day to keep a steady level in your system. If you miss a dose, skip it and take the next one at your regular time — never double up.
